newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Demand for lev funds remains low, depo rates flat.
newsitem.headline: Demand for lev funds remains low, depo rates flat.

text.p: Demand for lev funds was very low on Thursday as forex sales boosted banks' liquidity after the start of a fixed exchange rate regime two days ago, dealers said.

"Most market players prefer to boost their liquidity through foreign currency sales instead of bidding for funds on the interbank deposit market and placing foreign currency as collateral," said a dealer.
Traders said that banks have bought marks at lower levels in the past several weeks and now sell them to the central bank to profit from forex transaction costs.

The mark ask levels were between 900 and 950 levs in the weeks before the currency board was launched. The central bank was buying marks at 995 levs and selling at 1,000 levs under a fixed exchange rate regime launched on Tuesday.
Overnight interbank depo rates stood at 9-10 percent annually, flat from Wednesday, while deposits for up to seven days were borrowed at a simple annual interest of 7-8 percent, also unchanged.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 9.00 percent on Wednesday, a central bank official said.
The simple annual main interest rate is now set at 10.12 percent by the central bank. -- Dessislava Popova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
